items.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021
items.q: If you had brought home a record by Louis Jordan or some of the, you know the blues guys, would that have been accepted in your household?

ctx.x: I want to go back a little bit. Let’s say you were 13 or so, 1953, and your family was very into Gospel music. If you had brought home a record by Louis Jordan or some of the, you know the blues guys, would that have been accepted in your household?

Oh that’s why I was really blessed man, actually I’ve got two younger brothers who were very challenging. And my father played the four string guitar and he had a beautiful tenor voice. My two younger brothers got that tenor voice. But he loved music. He told me they would perform at the Apollo Theater and he would go, after that he would go listen to all the jazz groups, and he’d come back home and tell me about them and we’d go down in the basement and we’d listen to records, or back then you know the radio was…
